transcript.en: Your phone can run real Python, the same language used by scientists, game makers and banks. Today you will write your first program. It will be one line long. Today: your first Python program. The instruction print shows something on the screen. Put text inside quotes and brackets, exactly like this. Press Run, and the computer does exactly what you wrote. That’s a program! A program can have many lines. Python runs them one at a time, from the top down. Change the order of the lines, and the order on the screen changes too. Python is also a calculator. Plus and minus are as you know them. A star means times, and a slash means divide. Two stars mean to the power of: two, star star, ten is one thousand and twenty-four. Careful with quotes. With quotes, Python shows the text exactly as it is. Without quotes, it works the sum out. So the first line shows seven plus five, and the second shows twelve. Quick check! The line is print, two plus three times four, with no quotes. What does it show? Fourteen. Python follows the same order as maths: times and divide before plus and minus. If you want plus first, use brackets: two plus three, in brackets, times four is twenty. With just print and maths, you can already do useful things. Work out how many minutes are in a school year. Print a poster for a school event. Check your maths homework. Find out how many seconds old you are. Sometimes Python stops with a red error message. Don’t worry: everyone gets them. The last line says what’s wrong, and it tells you the line number. A missing quote or bracket is the most common. In the app, open Step through a program. Press Run and record, then Next, and watch Python run one line at a time. Then change the code to your own prints and sums, and run it again. Your turn. What does print, with ten times two in quotes, show? Ten times two, just as written. Remember: print shows things on the screen. Python runs your lines from top to bottom. Text goes in quotes. And times comes before plus, unless you use brackets. Try it yourself: work out how many hours you spend at school in a year, with one line of Python. Write your guess on paper first. Then run it, and see how close you were.

body.en:
A program is a list of instructions that a computer follows exactly, one line at a time, from the top down. In Python, print() shows something on the screen.

Text goes inside quotes: print("Hello!") shows Hello!. Python shows text exactly as written, so print("7 + 3") shows 7 + 3. Numbers and sums go without quotes, and Python works them out first: print(7 + 3) shows 10.

Python can calculate: + adds, - subtracts, * multiplies, / divides and ** is “to the power of” (2 ** 3 is 8). As in maths, * and / come before + and -, so use brackets when you want something else: (2 + 3) * 4 is 20. A comma in print() puts a space between the parts: print("Total:", 3 * 50).

If you make a mistake, Python stops and shows an error message with the line number. That is not a disaster. It’s a clue: read it, fix that line and run it again.
body.ar:
البرنامج قائمة تعليمات ينفّذها الحاسوب بالضبط، سطرًا بعد سطر، من الأعلى إلى الأسفل. وفي Python تُظهر ⁦print()⁩ شيئًا على الشاشة.

يوضع النص بين علامتَي تنصيص: ⁦print("Hello!")⁩ تُظهر ⁦Hello!⁩. وتُظهر Python النص كما كُتب تمامًا، فتُظهر ⁦print("7 + 3")⁩ النص ⁦7 + 3⁩. أمّا الأعداد والعمليات فتُكتب دون علامتَي تنصيص، وتحسبها Python أولًا: ⁦print(7 + 3)⁩ تُظهر 10.

تستطيع Python أن تحسب: + تجمع، و- تطرح، و* تضرب، و/ تقسم، و** تعني «أُسّ» (⁦2 ** 3⁩ تساوي 8). وكما في الرياضيات يأتي * و/ قبل + و-، فاستعمل الأقواس حين تريد غير ذلك: ⁦(2 + 3) * 4⁩ تساوي 20. والفاصلة داخل ⁦print()⁩ تضع مسافة بين الأجزاء: ⁦print("Total:", 3 * 50)⁩.

وإن أخطأت، تتوقّف Python وتُظهر رسالة خطأ معها رقم السطر. وهذه ليست كارثة، بل دليل: اقرأها، وأصلح ذلك السطر، وشغّله من جديد.

transcript.en: A game greets you by name, and knows your score. How does it remember? It keeps each thing in a variable, a name with a value inside. Today: variables, and programs that ask you questions. A variable is a name that holds a value. The equals sign puts the value on the right into the name on the left. After that, wherever you write the name, Python uses its value. A variable can change. Score equals score plus ten takes the old score, adds ten, and stores the new score. The old value is gone: a variable holds one value at a time. To ask the person using your program a question, use input. The program waits until they type an answer and press Enter. Store the answer in a variable, and use it. Here’s the trap. input always gives back text, even if you type a number. Text plus text sticks together: five plus three in quotes gives fifty-three! Turn the answer into a number with int, and the sum works. Quick check! Score is twenty. Then score equals score plus five. What does print score show? Twenty-five. In Python, the equals sign doesn’t mean the same as in maths. It means: work out the right side, then store it in the name on the left. Now your programs can talk back. Ask for a name and say hello. Ask for an age and say how old they’ll be in ten years. Ask for phone credit and a price, and say if there’s enough. Choose clear names: score, age, price. Names can’t have spaces, so use an underscore, like phone underscore credit. Capital letters count: Score and score are two different names. In the app, open Bug hunt and try bugs five and six. In one, a name is spelt wrong. In the other, text and a number are added together. Read the error, fix it and run it again. Your turn. A program asks your age with input, then prints age plus one. You type thirteen. What happens? An error. Remember: a variable is a name with one value at a time. The equals sign stores. input asks a question and always gives text. Use int to turn it into a number. Try it yourself: write a program that asks for your name and your age, then says how old you’ll be in ten years. Try it on a friend or someone at home!

body.en:
A variable is a name that holds a value, like a labelled box. score = 20 puts 20 into the box called score. Read = as “store”: the value on the right goes into the name on the left. A variable holds one value at a time, and you can change it: score = score + 5 takes the old score, adds 5 and stores the new one.

input() lets a program ask a question: name = input("Name? ") waits for an answer and stores it in name. But input() always gives back text, even when you type a number. So "5" + "3" is "53": two pieces of text joined together. To do maths with what was typed, turn it into a number with int(): age = int(input("Age? ")).

Two errors are common here. NameError means Python doesn’t know a name, often because of a typing mistake (scor instead of score). TypeError means you mixed text and numbers, such as "Age: " + 12. Read the message and its line: it tells you what to fix.
body.ar:
المتغيّر اسم يحمل قيمة، مثل صندوق عليه ملصق. فالسطر ⁦score = 20⁩ يضع 20 في الصندوق المسمّى score. واقرأ = على أنها «خزّن»: القيمة التي على اليمين تذهب إلى الاسم الذي على اليسار. ويحمل المتغيّر قيمة واحدة في كل مرة، وتستطيع تغييرها: ⁦score = score + 5⁩ تأخذ القيمة القديمة، وتضيف 5، وتخزّن القيمة الجديدة.

تسمح ⁦input()⁩ للبرنامج بأن يطرح سؤالًا: ⁦name = input("Name? ")⁩ تنتظر الإجابة وتخزّنها في name. لكن ⁦input()⁩ تعيد نصًّا دائمًا، حتى لو كتبت عددًا. ولهذا فإن ⁦"5" + "3"⁩ تساوي ⁦"53"⁩: قطعتا نص متّصلتان. ولكي تحسب بما كُتب، حوّله إلى عدد بـ ⁦int(): age = int(input("Age? "))⁩.

وهناك خطآن شائعان هنا. NameError يعني أن Python لا تعرف اسمًا، وغالبًا بسبب خطأ في الكتابة (scor بدل score). وTypeError يعني أنك خلطت نصًّا بعدد، مثل ⁦"Age: " + 12⁩. اقرأ الرسالة وسطرها: فهي تخبرك بما يجب إصلاحه.

transcript.en: At the science museum, children under twelve pay half price. The ticket machine decides your price in a blink. That decision is an if. Today: decisions in Python. A decision needs a question with a yes or no answer. Is age less than twelve? Python can compare with less than, greater than, two equals signs for the same, and exclamation equals for not the same. The answer is True or False. An if line asks the question and ends with a colon. The lines under it are pushed in by four spaces, and they run only if the answer is True. Under else go the lines for False. For more choices, add elif, short for else if. Under five, free. Under twelve, half price. Everyone else, full price. Python checks from the top and stops at the first True. You can join questions with and and or. With and, both must be True. With or, one is enough. A free ticket if you are under five or over seventy. Quick check! With that program, a girl who is exactly twelve buys a ticket. What does it print? Full price. Twelve is not less than twelve. Mistakes like this hide at the edges, so always test the boundary: eleven, twelve and thirteen. The most common bug: one equals sign stores, two equals signs compare. If you write if age equals twelve with one sign, Python stops with a syntax error. Inside an if, you almost always need two. Decisions make programs smart. A quiz that says correct or try again. A game that ends when your lives reach zero. A phone that warns you when the battery is low. In the app, open Logic gates. Try AND and OR with two switches, and watch when the lamp lights. Then solve the Door alarm: door or window open, and the alarm switched on. Your turn. Age is fifteen. What is age greater than twelve, and age less than eighteen: True or False? True. Remember: a comparison is True or False. if runs its indented lines only when True; else covers the rest; elif adds choices. Two equals signs compare. And test the boundaries. body.en:
A decision starts with a comparison. Python has six: == (equal to), != (not equal to), < (less than), > (greater than), <= and >= (less than or equal to, greater than or equal to). Each one is either True or False. Watch out: one = stores a value, two == compare.

if runs its lines only when the condition is True. else catches everything else. elif (“else if”) adds more choices in between. Python checks from the top and runs only the first branch that is true. Every if, elif and else line ends with a colon, and the lines that belong to it are indented by 4 spaces.

You can join conditions. and needs both to be true: age >= 13 and age <= 19 is a teenager. or needs only one: day == "Saturday" or day == "Sunday".

Test your decisions at the boundaries, the values where the answer changes. If under 12 pays half, try 11, 12 and 13.
body.ar:
يبدأ القرار بمقارنة. وفي Python ست مقارنات: == (يساوي)، و⁦!=⁩ (لا يساوي)، و⁦<⁩ (أصغر من)، و⁦>⁩ (أكبر من)، و⁦<=⁩ و⁦>=⁩ (أصغر من أو يساوي، أكبر من أو يساوي). ونتيجة كلٍّ منها True أو False. وانتبه: علامة = الواحدة تخزّن قيمة، والعلامتان == تقارنان.

تنفّذ if أسطرها فقط حين يكون الشرط True، وتلتقط else كل ما عدا ذلك. أمّا elif («else if») فتضيف اختيارات بينهما. وتفحص Python من الأعلى وتنفّذ أول فرع صحيح فقط. وكل سطر if أو elif أو else ينتهي بنقطتين رأسيتين، وتُزاح الأسطر التابعة له ٤ مسافات.

وتستطيع ربط الشروط. فـ and تحتاج إلى صحّة الاثنين: ⁦age >= 13 and age <= 19⁩ مراهق. وor تحتاج إلى واحد فقط: ⁦day == "Saturday" or day == "Sunday"⁩.

transcript.en: When I was at school, a punishment was writing a line a hundred times. My hand hurt for days! Python would do it in two lines, in less than a second. Today: loops, and how to repeat without getting tired. A for loop repeats the lines inside it. range of five gives five turns. The indented line runs once for each turn. Change five to a hundred, and it runs a hundred times. The loop variable counts for you. range of one, six gives one, two, three, four and five: it stops just before six. Use it to print a countdown, a times table or numbered seats. A loop can add up as it goes. Start total at zero. Each time round, add the next number. After the loop, total holds the answer: one plus two plus three plus four is ten. A while loop repeats as long as its question is True. It’s perfect when you don’t know how many turns you’ll need, like a guessing game: keep asking until the guess is right. Quick check! A loop says for i in range of three, and inside it, print Hello. How many times is Hello printed? Three times. range of three starts at zero and stops before three: zero, one, two. Python often counts from zero, so get used to it! Careful with while. If its question never becomes False, the loop never stops. Darsi stops your program after three seconds, so your phone won’t freeze. Then look for what should change inside the loop. Loops can search, too. Checking one number after another is a for loop. A smarter way halves the range each time: guess the middle, then keep the half where the number must be. That’s a while loop. In the app, open Guess the number. With one to a hundred, press only Try the middle: you never need more than seven guesses. Then race one by one against halving, up to a thousand. Your turn. Total starts at zero, and a loop adds each number in range of one, four. What is the total at the end? Six. Remember: for repeats once for each value in a range. range stops before its end, and often starts at zero. A total starts at zero before the loop. while repeats until its question is False. Try it yourself: write a guess-the-number game with a while loop, and play it with a friend or someone at home. Count how many guesses they need, and teach them the halving trick!

Hello هتتطبع كام مرة؟ تلات مرات. range لتلاتة بتبدأ من صفر وبتقف قبل التلاتة: صفر، وواحد، واتنين. بايثون كتير بيعدّ من صفر، فاتعوّد على كده! خلّي بالك من الـ while. لو السؤال بتاعها عمره ما بقى False، اللوب عمره ما هيقف. درسي بيوقّف برنامجك بعد تلات ثواني، فموبايلك مش هيهنّج. وبعدين دوّر على الحاجة اللي المفروض تتغيّر جوّه اللوب. اللوب كمان يقدر يدوّر. إنك تشيّك رقم ورا رقم ده لوب for. وفيه طريقة أذكى بتقسم المدى نصين كل مرة: خمّن النص، وبعدين خلّي النص اللي لازم الرقم يكون فيه. ودي لوب while. في التطبيق، افتح «خمّن الرقم». من واحد لمية، دوس بس «جرّب المنتصف»: عمرك ما هتحتاج أكتر من سبع تخمينات. وبعدين سابق بين واحد واحد والقسمة على اتنين، لحد ألف. دورك. total بيبدأ بصفر، ولوب بيزوّد كل رقم في range واحد، أربعة. المجموع في الآخر كام؟ ستة. افتكر: الـ for بتكرر مرة لكل قيمة في الـ range. والـ range بتقف قبل آخرها، وكتير بتبدأ من صفر. والمجموع بيبدأ بصفر قبل اللوب. والـ while بتكرر لحد ما السؤال يبقى False. جرّبها بنفسك: اكتب لعبة خمّن الرقم بلوب while، والعبها مع صاحبك أو حد في البيت. عدّ هما احتاجوا كام تخمينة، وعلّمهم حيلة القسمة على اتنين!

body.en:
Writing print a hundred times would take for ever. A loop repeats lines for you. for repeats once for each value: for i in range(1, 6): runs its indented lines five times, with i set to 1, 2, 3, 4 and then 5. range(a, b) starts at a and stops just before b. range(5) means range(0, 5): 0 to 4.

Loops can count and add up. Start with total = 0 before the loop. Inside it, total = total + i adds each value. After the loop, total holds the sum.

while repeats as long as its condition is True: while guess != secret: keeps asking until the right number is guessed. Something inside the loop must change, or it never ends. A loop that never ends is a common bug, and on your phone Python stops it after 3 seconds.

Searching uses loops too. Checking one by one can take as many guesses as there are numbers; halving (guess the middle, then throw away the wrong half) finds a number from 1 to 100 in 7 guesses or fewer.
body.ar:
كتابة print مئة مرة ستأخذ وقتًا طويلًا جدًا. أمّا الحلقة فتكرّر الأسطر عنك. فـ for تتكرّر مرة لكل قيمة: ⁦for i in range(1, 6):⁩ تنفّذ أسطرها المُزاحة خمس مرات، وتأخذ i القيم 1 و2 و3 و4 ثم 5. وتبدأ ⁦range(a, b)⁩ من a وتتوقّف قبل b مباشرة. وتعني ⁦range(5)⁩ الشيء نفسه مثل ⁦range(0, 5)⁩: من 0 إلى 4.

وتستطيع الحلقات أن تعدّ وتجمع. ابدأ بـ ⁦total = 0⁩ قبل الحلقة، وفي داخلها تضيف ⁦total = total + i⁩ كل قيمة. وبعد الحلقة يحمل total المجموع.

أمّا while فتتكرّر ما دام شرطها True: ⁦while guess != secret:⁩ تستمرّ في السؤال حتى يُخمَّن الرقم الصحيح. ويجب أن يتغيّر شيء داخل الحلقة، وإلّا لا تنتهي أبدًا. والحلقة التي لا تنتهي خطأ شائع، وعلى هاتفك توقفها Python بعد ٣ ثوانٍ.

والبحث يستعمل الحلقات أيضًا. فالفحص واحدًا واحدًا قد يحتاج إلى عدد تخمينات يساوي عدد الأرقام، أمّا التنصيف (خمّن الوسط، ثم استبعد النصف الخطأ) فيجد رقمًا من ١ إلى ١٠٠ في ٧ تخمينات أو أقل.

hints.en: if a > b: print(a), else: print(b), each print indented.
hints.ar: ⁦if a > b:⁩ ثم ⁦print(a)⁩، و⁦else:⁩ ثم ⁦print(b)⁩، وكل print مُزاحة.

explain.en: One comparison decides which mark to print. When they are equal, a > b is False, so else prints b, which is the same mark.
explain.ar: مقارنة واحدة تقرّر أيّ الدرجتين تُطبع. وحين تتساويان يكون ⁦a > b⁩ خطأ، فتطبع else الدرجة b، وهي الدرجة نفسها.

prompt.en: if score = 10: is a correct line of Python.
prompt.ar: ⁦if score = 10:⁩ سطر صحيح في Python.

explain.en: Comparing needs ==: if score == 10:. A single = stores a value and is a SyntaxError inside an if.
explain.ar: المقارنة تحتاج إلى ==: ⁦if score == 10:⁩. أمّا = الواحدة فتخزّن قيمة، وتسبّب SyntaxError داخل if.

en: Warm-up (3 min): Write one thing you learned in each of the four lessons, in your own words.
Make (7 min): In pairs, write a quiz program on paper: it asks three questions with input(), uses if to check each answer, and keeps a score.
Swap (7 min): Swap with another pair. Predict what their program prints for some answers, and look for bugs.
Run (3 min): Type one quiz into the phone and play it. Did it behave as predicted?
ar: التمهيد (٣ دقائق): اكتب بكلماتك شيئًا تعلّمته في كل درس من الدروس الأربعة.
الصنع (٧ دقائق): في أزواج، اكتبوا على الورق برنامج اختبار: يطرح ثلاثة أسئلة بـ ⁦input()⁩، ويستعمل if ليفحص كل إجابة، ويحتفظ بالنتيجة.
التبادل (٧ دقائق): تبادلوا البرنامج مع زوج آخر. وتوقّعوا ما يطبعه لبعض الإجابات، وابحثوا عن الأخطاء.
التشغيل (٣ دقائق): اكتبوا اختبارًا واحدًا في الهاتف والعبوه. هل تصرّف كما توقّعتم؟
